name: infection control overview
title: Infection control decision chart: routine practices and hand hygiene for every patient, then the route of transmission picks the additional precautions: contact, droplet, droplet plus contact, droplet plus contact with enhanced protective equipment for an aerosol-generating procedure, or airborne; each column gives example infections and the precautions, and the order to put on and take off protective equipment runs under all of them

root.title: Possibly infectious patient: ROUTINE practices for everyone, then which ROUTE decides the extra precautions?
lines: ROUTINE, every patient: risk assessment · hand hygiene at the 4 moments · personal protective equipment (PPE) for the exposure you expect
hands VISIBLY soiled → soap and water · otherwise alcohol-based hand rub

groups.title: TOUCH
lines: the person, or an object they contaminated

groups.title: DROPLETS: ≥ 5 μm, fall within 2 m
lines: from coughs and sneezes onto the nose, mouth or eyes

groups.title: AIRBORNE: < 5 μm
lines: carried far on air currents: hardest to control

head: h
Contact
direct or indirect
ex: • C. difficile, methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales
tx: dedicated equipment, or disinfect it before the next patient

head: h
Droplet
tx: Face mask + eye protection within 2 m
patient wears a surgical mask for transport

head: h
Droplet + contact
tx: Gloves, gown, face mask, eye protection

head: h
Droplet + contact, ENHANCED PPE
for an aerosol-generating medical procedure (AGMP)
tx: Gloves, level 2 gown, N95, full-face visor
